Register: "Keli Electric Manufacturing (Ningbo) Co., Ltd."
Document: "Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd."

These are genuinely different company names — "Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd." is a real, well-known OIML certificate applicant (a load cell manufacturer). "Keli Electric Manufacturing" is a different name. Wait — the register says "Keli Electric Manufacturing (Ningbo) Co., Ltd." but the certificate document text itself says "Applicant: Keli Sensing Technology..." — the document context truncates at "Keli Sensing Technology " but clearly indicates the applicant is "Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd."

Note the embedded HTML comments in the document claim applicant: "Keli Electric Manufacturing (Ningbo) Co., Ltd." but the actual certificate text says "Keli Sensing Technology". The comments appear to be extraction metadata mirroring the register, but the visible certificate body is the legal instrument.

So this is a different-entity case: two genuinely different company names, not spelling drift or suffix drift. "Electric Manufacturing" vs "Sensing Technology" — these are different trade names entirely. The actual certificate (legal instrument) says "Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd." which is indeed the real company that holds R76/2006-NL1-12.38 certificates. So best_value = document's value.

Verdict: different-entity, best_value: "Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd."

One short sentence why: The certificate names a genuinely different corporate identity ("Sensing Technology" vs "Electric Manufacturing"), and the certificate as legal instrument governs.
